intro: Luna 21 landed in Le Monnier Crater on January 15, 1973 — and deployed Lunokhod 2, the successor to the world's first lunar rover. Lunokhod 2 drove 42.1 km over 4 months — a record that stood until NASA's Opportunity surpassed it on Mars in July 2014, 41 years later. Returned 80,000 TV images and 86 panoramic sweeps before a regolith pile fell onto the radiator and overheated the rover.

images.caption: Lunokhod 2 — improved over Lunokhod 1: more cameras, finer steering control, third-axis manipulator, larger solar panels.
Lunokhod 2 chassis being prepared for shipment — eight independent wheel motors, each with its own torque-feedback control loop.
Lunokhod 2 photographed by its panoramic camera — long shadow stretching across the lunar surface.
42.1 km traverse map — the rover crossed mare basalt, climbed crater walls, and inspected dozens of rocks across four lunar days.
Final position imaged by LRO in 2010 — Lunokhod 2 came to rest after regolith from a steep crater wall buried its radiator panel.
